title: Skate or Die!
build: PAL, two-sided G64 pair supplied by the contributor (side 1 SHA-256 45e07b32..., side 2 7a402586...); EA loader, no crack or trainer

records.c: 6510 data-direction register; the shop never writes it (its zero-page clear starts at $13)
6510 processor port: the shop writes $25 (RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O at $D000-$DFFF) at $0F4B, $0FED and $0B9E, and the raster interrupt saves it, sets $25 and restores it ($11B3-$11E2)

Load stub, copied here by the resident event manager (run_load_stub $FA58 copies 29 bytes, $0800-$081C, from its template at $F925, patched per load). This copy loaded the shop: file $03 through JSR $F230 with X/Y = $0880 ($0880-$26FF), then CIA 1 port A as outputs, port B as inputs, $7F on port A (keyboard row 7), and JMP $0880. $081C is the template's 29th byte ($AD); $081D-$087F are zero and unused

SHOP AND TOWN PROGRAM (file $03, loaded at $0880-$26FF by the event manager's load stub, entered here). Resets the stack, runs shop_init ($093B: loads files $04-$0A, unpacks the pictures, sets up the raster interrupt), enables interrupts and enters the main loop at $0887. The main loop does only the slow work: each pass it services the screen-redraw requests that the interrupt-side input handlers raise ($41 shop picture, $42 board-colour screen, $43 skater list for a board, $44 name entry, $45 sign-in list, $48 records), checks whether the skater has left the town for an event ($08A2), and updates Rodney's speech balloon ($0C1D). All input, movement and sprite work runs in the raster interrupt ($11AD). The program has no sound: nothing in it writes the SID

Main loop: shop_redraw_request $0BF0, colour_screen_request $0D50, board_list_request $0C62, name_entry_request $0DD4, signin_list_request $0E2E, records_request $0CA9, leave_town_check $08A2, update_speech $0C1D, then round again. Each request routine returns at once unless its flag is set

Called every main-loop pass. $47 is the destination the town movement code ($17D2-$1887) set when the skater rolled off an edge of the square (1 RAMP, 2 HIGH JUMP, 3 DOWNHILL, 4 JAM, 5 POOL JOUST, the event manager's row numbers). Nothing to do while it is 0. If no skater has signed in (num_skaters $F897 = 0) and the town is not in practice (practice_flag $FE11 = 0), the event is refused: mode 8, the message MUST REGISTER AT SKATESHOP ($20BB) on the text screen at row 11, column 7, the skater put back in front of the shop at x $4B, y $54, speed 0, sprites moved off, and $47 cleared; fire returns to the square ($1DA8). Otherwise go_to_event ($08F9)

Leave for the event in $47: clear archive_scores ($FD7A, 36 bytes) and archive_ids ($FD9E, 12), zero overall_points ($FD72) and set skater_ids ($FDAA) to 0-7, so every departure from the town starts a new set of results; then store $47 in cur_event ($F893), switch the sprites and the raster interrupt off, write 0 to $7FFF (the VIC's idle byte in bank 1) and jump to the event manager's goto_event ($F99C) with X = the destination. $0935 stores A into $47 meaning to clear it, but A holds the value just read from $D019, not 0; harmless, since the zero-page clear at start-up ($0977) runs before $47 is read again
Unreachable RTS after the JMP at $0937

Start-up, called once from shop_entry with interrupts off: save $D018/$DD00/$D021 ($10D8, never read back), zero the program's variables $2681-$26A3, X and Y expansion off for all sprites, point the NMI and IRQ vectors at the RTI at $0A3A, clear zero page $13-$DF, load and unpack the files ($0F46), set CIA 1 for the keyboard (port A outputs, port B inputs, row 7 selected), select VIC bank 1 ($DD00 bits = %10) with $D018 = $BE (screen $6C00, characters $7800). Mode $26A4: 1 (shop) if the load routine set it (first boot) or after a full competition (comp_flag), otherwise 0 (town). Build the sprites ($0A95, $0A3B), put the town skater at x $50, y $70, start the raster interrupt at line $FB ($10E8), then, after a full competition, find the skater with the most overall points ($FD72; on a tie the later skater) and copy the first 9 characters of the name into the CONGRATS line at $2457 (a zero shows as a space), with $26A3 set so Rodney says it. Clear comp_flag and quit_flag ($FE12), install the IRQ at $11AD, band 0, border black, clear the text screen ($0BBE), set the print base to $6C00 and, in the shop, enter it ($1B60)
Zero $2681-$26A3, the sprite shadow registers and the menu variables (the loop stops at $26A4, the mode byte, which keeps the file's $84 until $09A3)
Operand byte ($14) of the LDA $14 at $0953 inside the variable clear; the symbol here comes from the RESET vector at $FFFC, which holds $0954 from older code, not from anything in the shop

RTI, the do-nothing interrupt handler: shop_init points the NMI vector $FFFA and the IRQ vector $FFFE here ($0967-$0974) while it loads; $FFFE is moved on to raster_irq ($11AD) at $0A11, $FFFA stays, so a RESTORE key press returns at once. The events inherit this NMI vector

Sprite colours and multicolour flags: all eight sprites enabled ($269A = $FF), sprite multicolours $0B and $00, sprites 0-2 and 4 coloured from $2503-$2506 (orange, white, blue, black: the town skater's body parts), sprite 3 (the board) from skater_attr ($FCD2) of skater 0; multicolour on for sprites 1 and 2, off for 0, 3 and 4; x positions of sprites 0-6 zeroed so nothing shows until a screen places them

Clear the six speech-balloon sprite blocks ($8440-$84FF and $8500-$85BF) and copy the 64-byte pointer sprite from $2641 to $8400 (sprite pointer $10 in VIC bank 2): the small SKATE / OR / DIE! logo that serves as the shop's pointer

Merge the last competition's results into the high-score table at $9900 (file $08). Skipped when nobody has signed in. For each archived event 1-4 (RAMP FREESTYLE, RAMP HIGHJUMP, DOWNHILL RACE, DOWNHILL JAM; $4C = 0, 3, 6, 9, the event's first record) it calls merge_event ($0ACA). Any insertion sets $49, which makes check_records ($0B9C) save the table to disk ($0BB4) and the raster interrupt show the records screen ($18F5), unless a full competition just ended (shop_init clears $49 at $09D5 when comp_flag is set)

Merge one event's top three (archive_scores $FD7A + 3*($4C+k), k = $4E) into its three records (slots $4C+j, j = $4D) like a merge of two sorted lists: a record's 24-bit score ($990A-$990C, low byte first) is compared with archived score k; if the record is greater or equal the next record is tried, otherwise score k is inserted at slot j ($0B0D) and the next archived score is taken. Stops after three insertions or three slots. An archived score equal to a record does not displace it, so the earlier holder keeps the place

Insert archived score $4E at record slot $4D of the event at $4C: set the changed flag $49, move the records below down one place (slot 1 to 2, then slot 0 to 1, via $0B87), look the archived skater id (archive_ids $FD9E) up in skater_ids ($FDAA) to find the skater's name, copy its first 9 characters into the record (+0-+8) with a zero at +9, the three score bytes at +$0A-$0C, and colour 7 (yellow) at +$0F, so the new record stands out on the records screen. Names are cut to 9 characters
Not found: the archived id is in no ranking slot. The program stops here for good, flashing the border (INC $D020 forever), an assertion trap
Copy the 16-byte record at slot $4C+A to slot $4C+A+1 ($9900+16n to $9910+16n), making room for an insertion
Called by load_files at start-up: RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF ($01 = $25), merge the records ($0AB2) and, if any changed ($49), save them ($0BB4)
Nine bytes no code reaches ($BD $DA $FC $FF $00 $30 $60 $90 $FF): the start of an LDA $FCDA,X and other fragments, left between two routines

Write the 192-byte record table $9900-$99BF back to the disk as file $08 through the resident loader's save_file ($F233, A = 8, X/Y = $9900). The only call of save_file in the game's resident code or this program: the high scores live on the disk (file $08, track 35)
Fill the hires text screen $6C00-$6FE7 (1000 bytes) with spaces through $14/$15; used at start-up and by the MUST REGISTER message

The same fill of $6C00-$6FE7 with spaces through $1C/$1D instead of $14/$15, so it can run from the input handlers inside the raster interrupt without disturbing a pointer the main loop is using. Called whenever a menu switches screen, leaving a blank screen while the main loop builds the next one

Main loop: when $41 is set (the skater entered the shop door, $18E9, or a menu returned to the shop, $1B92), copy the shop picture's colours $9C00-$9FFF to colour RAM ($10A2), set the speech index $72 to $FF (none), put the pointer at x $4E, y $74, switch to mode 2 (shop with pointer), clear practice_flag ($FE11) and clear $41. The bitmap itself ($A000) and its screen ($8000) never change, so entering the shop only costs the colour copy

Main loop, in the shop (mode 2): when the hotspot under the pointer ($72, from find_hotspot $1EB6) differs from the one last drawn ($26A0), draw the new line into the speech balloon. No hotspot ($FF) gives line $13 (blank), or line $14 (CONGRATS <name> YER TOP SKATER!!!) once after a full competition ($26A3). Bit 7 of the hotspot (talk only) is dropped; hotspot $0B picks one of eight lines $0B-$12 at random (random_step $F90F AND 7). The line's address comes from $2154/$2169 and draw_speech ($0EA9) renders it

Main loop: when $43 is set (CHANGE BOARD COLOR chosen, $1A7E), build the board menu on screen $7000 from the template at $8800 (colours $E400), list the skaters ($0E7C) and print CANCEL ($20A2) in colour 2 on the row after the last skater; clear $43. Mode 3 (set by the caller) then moves the cursor

Main loop: when $48 is set, draw the records screen on $7000 from the template at $6800 (colours $E800) and print the twelve records from $9900: record x at column $207E[x], row $208A[x], in the colour stored at +$0F (then reset to 3, cyan, so a new record is yellow only the first time it is shown); the name from +0, then the score at column +10: three BCD bytes +$0C, +$0B, +$0A as six digits for records 0-2 and 6-11, and for records 3-5 (high jump) +$0B, a ' , +$0A and a " for feet and inches. Clears $48
High jump records (3-5): feet from +$0B, the ' (screen code $27), inches from +$0A, the " ($22)

Main loop: when $42 is set, build the board-colour screen: cursor limits for fifteen colours ($75 = 15, $76 = 14, first row $77 = 10), template $6400 with colours $EC00 copied to $7000, the selected skater's name ($FCDA + 16*$7B) printed in yellow on row 6, centred on column 19, then mode 5, the town skater placed at x $48, y $9A facing heading 8 so that the band-1 interrupt draws him on the right as a preview in the board colour, and the cursor $72 on the skater's colour - 1. Clears $42

Main loop: when $44 is set (fire on a slot of the sign-in list), redraw the sign-in screen (template $8800, colours $E400), mark the slot being typed with > at column 8 and < at column 27 on its row (unless it is the ninth row), clear $26A1 (nothing typed yet), list the skaters and clear $44 and the typing state $78-$7A (length, key, last key). Mode 6 (set by $1BA0) reads the keyboard

Main loop: when $45 is set (SIGN IN chosen, $1CEC), draw the sign-in screen (template $8800, colours $E400), list the skaters and print CANCEL in colour 2 two rows below the first empty slot (with eight skaters, on row 24 straight after the last name), then clear $45
Print the eight skater names (skater_names $FCDA, 16 bytes apart) in white at column 12, rows 8, 10 ... 22 of the screen at $26/$27; an empty slot prints nothing

Render a 36-character line at ($14) into the speech balloon's six sprites: each character (AND $3F) selects an 8x8 glyph at $7800 + 8*code, whose 8 bytes go into the sprite rows 3 bytes apart starting at the offset from $0F0B for that character position. The first 18 characters go to the sprites at $8440-$84FF, the next 18 (the STA operand at $0EE7/$0EE8 is moved to $8500) to $8500-$85BF: four lines of nine characters, two lines per row of three sprites
Operand of the STA $FFFF,X at $0EE6, written at $0EAB/$0EB0 ($8440) and $0EFD/$0F02 ($8500): the sprite block the glyph rows go to
High byte of speech_dest_ptr: $84 for the first 18 characters, $85 for the rest

36 offsets, one per character of a speech line, into the balloon's sprite blocks: 0, 1, 2 (first sprite), $40-$42 (second), $80-$82 (third) for a line's nine characters, then $18-$1A, $58-$5A, $98-$9A for the next line eight sprite rows lower; the pattern repeats for the second half, which goes to the lower row of sprites
Before the record file loads, fill the 192 bytes at $9900 with zeros and colour $0E at +$0F of each 16-byte record. The load retries until it succeeds ($0F64), so the file always overwrites this

Load the program's files with the resident load_file ($F230) from the table at $20F2 (file) / $20F9 (address low) / $2100 (high), retrying each on a drive error: $04 to $6184 (town and screens, packed), $05 to $7800 (font), $06 to $8800 (sign-in screen and skater sprites), $07 to $E5F4 (colour maps, packed), $08 to $9900 (high scores), $09 to $AB1D (shop picture, packed), $0A to $8000 (shop picture's screen). If the event manager is not in memory yet (manager_installed $FDFF is not $55, the first load after the title), the screen is blanked after file $08, file $0B is loaded to $C000 and copied up to $F730 ($0FD2), the border colour is stepped once and the start mode set to 1, the shop. Then unpack the three packed files ($0FEA), set the record colours ($1089), merge and save records ($0B9C), zero event_scores ($107E), copy the town's colours to colour RAM ($109A) and switch the screen back on
Copy X + 256*Y bytes from ($14) to ($16) one byte at a time (fetch_src $1068, store_dst $1073); with X = 0 exactly Y pages
First load only: copy file $0B from $C000 to $F730, $08C8 bytes ($F730-$FFF7), installing the resident event manager. So the shop, not the title or the boot, puts the event manager in place

Unpack the three run-length packed files where they were loaded: $6184-$77FF (file $04) to $4000-$6BE7 (the town bitmap, its screen and two text-screen templates), $E5F4-$EFFF (file $07) to $E000-$EFEF (four colour maps), $AB1D-$BFFF (file $09) to $9C00-$BF3F (the shop picture's colours and bitmap). Each unpacks in place, the output starting below the packed data and never catching it up

Run-length unpacker, the same format as High Jump's $1B6A: from ($14) to ($16) until $14/$15 reaches $1A/$1B. A control byte $00-$7F copies the next n + 1 bytes; $80-$FF repeats the next byte n - $7F times (1 to 128)
A = the byte at ($14), then step $14/$15
Store A at ($16), then step $16/$17
Zero event_scores ($FD5A-$FD71), the 24 result bytes of the eight skaters

Set the colour byte (+$0F) of every record to 3 (cyan) before merging, so only records inserted by this load are yellow. The loop steps X by 16 from $0F until it reaches $EF, so it also writes $99CF and $99DF, two bytes past the twelfth record ($99BF); nothing uses those bytes
Copy the town picture's colours $E000-$E3FF to colour RAM $D800-$DBFF; falls into $10A2

Copy four pages from ($14) to colour RAM $D800-$DBFF; the shop picture ($9C00), the text-screen colour maps ($E400, $E800, $EC00) and the town ($E000) each have 1000 colours and 24 spare bytes, which land in the unused colour RAM after $DBE7
Copy four pages from ($14) to the text screen $7000-$73FF: the template of the next menu screen ($8800 sign-in and board lists, $6400 board colours, $6800 records)
Keep $D018, $DD00 and $D021 in $7C, $7E and $7D at start-up; nothing reads them back
Turn CIA 1's interrupts off, wait for the top of the frame ($110A), set the raster compare to line $FB (bit 8 clear), enable the raster interrupt alone, and wait for the next frame top

Wait for the start of a frame: loop until $D012 changes to a value below the old one as a signed byte difference (CMP then BMI); a step of one line always loops again, so the exit comes when the count wraps from line 311 ($37) to 0
Put screen code A at column $2A, row $2B of the screen at $26/$27 (row start from the tables $25EF/$2608), with colour $28 in the matching colour-RAM cell, then step the column. Keeps Y

Print the zero-terminated text at ($14) from column $2A, row $2B, in colour $28: ASCII capitals $41-$5A become screen codes 1-26, other bytes (digits, punctuation, and names already held as screen codes) go out unchanged. Keeps Y
The RTS that ends print_string, also the do-nothing handler that the joystick tables give for impossible stick positions (up with down, left with right)

Print the BCD byte A as two characters from $2631 ("0123456789", then A-F for non-decimal nibbles) with leading-zero suppression: $2E records that a non-zero byte has been seen (a zero byte before that prints as two blanks), $2D that a non-zero digit has been printed (a zero high digit before that is a blank). Callers clear both before a number and set $2E before its last byte so that a zero still prints one 0. Keeps Y

Raster interrupt, the whole of the program's real-time work. Saves A, X, Y and the port $01, maps RAM in ($01 = $25: RAM at $A000-$BFFF and $E000-$FFFF, I/O visible), acknowledges the VIC, takes band $1F's handler from $2096 (patching the JSR at $11DE), moves $1F on to the next band ($209C) and sets that band's line ($209A), re-enables interrupts and calls the handler. Two bands: band 0 at line $FA (below the picture) runs band0_irq ($11EA), band 1 at line $2F (above it) runs band1_irq ($12EC)
Operand of the JSR at $11DE, written from $2096/$2097 at $11C7/$11CD: the current band's handler, $11EA or $12EC
High byte of irq_handler_ptr

Band 0, at raster line $FA: select VIC bank 1 and set the video mode for the top of the next frame from the mode byte $26A4 (skipped while new records wait to be shown, $49): modes 3, 6, 7 (board list, name entry, sign-in list) multicolour text from screen $7000 with characters $7800 ($D018 = $CE), background $0C, $0F, $0B; mode 9 (records) the same with $06, $0E, $00; modes 1 and 2 (shop) multicolour bitmap in VIC bank 2 (bitmap $A000, screen $8000); all other modes (0 town, 4, 5 colours, 8 message) hires text from $6C00 ($D018 = $BE) on black. Then, every frame: copy the sprite shadows to the VIC ($137B), read the joystick and run the mode's handler ($18F1), turn the skater ($1712), move him ($172F), and step the event manager's random generator ($F90F) so that its sequence depends on how long the player spends here
Modes 3, 6, 7: screen $7000, characters $7800, text mode, multicolour on, background colours $0C (grey), $0F (light grey), $0B (dark grey)
Mode 9, the records screen: multicolour text from $7000 like $124D, with background colours $06 (blue), $0E (light blue), $00 (black)
Modes 1 and 2: VIC bank 2 ($DD00 bits = %01), $D018 = $08 (screen $8000, bitmap $A000), multicolour bitmap mode, background black, $D022/$D023 $0E and $00

Band 1, at raster line $2F, just above the first visible line: in mode 0 (town) switch on the multicolour bitmap at $4000 with screen $6000 ($D018 = $80) and draw the skater ($13C0); in mode 5 (board colour) switch to the text screen at $7000 ($D018 = $CE, hires, as band 0 left it) and draw the skater as the colour preview; mode 3 sets $D018 = $CE and multicolour; modes 1 and 2 the shop bitmap again. Nothing while new records wait ($49). In modes 4 and 8 band 0's hires text from $6C00 stays for the whole frame, which is how the blank screen between menus and the MUST REGISTER message are shown

Never called: if $3E is set, clear it and move the town skater one step left ($2F - 1, not below 0). $3E and $3F are written nowhere else; an earlier way of moving the skater, superseded by move_skater ($172F)
Never called: if $3F is set, clear it and move the town skater one step right ($2F + 1, not past $98)

Copy the sprite shadow registers to the VIC every frame: x and y of sprites 0-7 from $2681-$2688 and $2689-$2690, the pointers from $2691-$2698 into all four screens in use ($63F8 town, $6FF8 text, $73F8 menus, $83F8 shop), the x high bits ($2699), enable ($269A), priority ($269B) and multicolour ($269C), and sprite 3's colour from skater_attr of the selected skater ($7B), the board colour

Draw the town skater as five sprites (0-4), from band1_irq in the town and on the board-colour screen. Flips the double buffer $63, picks the frames from the heading: $68 = 15 - (((heading + $34 - 2) / 4) AND 15) for the legs and board (parts 2-4: frames $20, $30, $40 + $68) and $67 = ($68 - turn rate $36) AND 15 for the body (parts 0 and 1: frames $67 and $10 + $67), so the body leads into a turn; $34 is never written, so 0. Copies the shapes ($1516), then sets x = $18 + 2 * $2F + each part's x offset as a 9-bit position (the high bits in $2699) and y = $32 + $30 + each part's y offset. Returns at once in mode 2, which never calls it

For parts 0-4: frame $5C+i selects a 6-byte record at $8C00 + 6*frame; copy_shape ($1698) copies the shape into the part's sprite block, $7400 + $80*i plus $40 in the second buffer ($2501[$63]), and returns its x and y offsets, kept in $57-$5B and $52-$56. Then the pointers $D0 + 2i + $63 go to $2691-$2695

Frame record at ($18): +0/+1 the shape's offset from $8DE0, +2 its length - 1, +3 the x offset, +4 the y offset (+5 is not read). Copies the shape's bytes into the sprite block whose address is already patched into $16BE/$16C7, zero-fills the rest of the 64 bytes, and returns the offsets in $61 and $62. Shapes are stored trimmed to the rows they use, as in High Jump
Operand of the LDA $969B,Y at $16BA, written at $169F/$16A7 with $8DE0 + the frame's shape offset
High byte of shape_src_ptr

Operand of the STA $7640,Y at $16BD, written with the part's sprite block by build_sprite_parts; the same address is patched into the STA at $16C6 ($16C7/$16C8), which zero-fills the rest of the block
High byte of shape_dst_ptr ($74-$76)
Operand of the STA $7640,Y at $16C6 that zero-fills the rest of the sprite block; written with the same address as $16BE
High byte of the zero-fill STA operand, the same block page as $16BF

Add the turn rate $36 (-1, 0 or +1) to the accumulator $6D and step the heading $31 by one for every 2 it collects, so a held turn turns one step every second frame (64 steps, a whole circle in 128 frames). The heading runs from -31 to +32 ($E1-$20): 0 faces down the screen, +16 right, +32 up, -16 left; stepping past +32 continues at -31 and past -31 at +32. $69 gets the absolute value

Turn ($16CF), then take the step for the heading: dx = $24D0[|h|] and dy = $24E0[|h|], dx negated for a negative heading. The two tables overlap and describe a diamond, |dx| + |dy| = 16, not a circle: a diagonal step is 8 and 8, about 70 % of the straight-line distance per frame

Move the town skater speed ($32, 0-3) times per frame: add dx to the x fraction $70 and dy to the y fraction $6F, and each time one passes +$30 or -$30 take it back and try one step right, left, down or up ($1793, $17E2, $1839, $1888), which either moves the position ($2F counts 2 pixels, $30 one line), stops at a wall, or sets the destination $47 at an edge. Stops early once the shop door has been entered ($41). The speed is kept until the stick is pulled back: there is no friction, and a wall stops the movement without changing the speed

One step right: at the right edge (x = $98) choose RAMP ($47 = 1) above y $28 or HIGH JUMP ($47 = 2) below it; otherwise refuse the step if a wall's left side is at this x for this y (x $25 or $4F above y $6C, the shop front; x $29 at y $90 and below; x $7D at y $98 and below; x $81 between y $27 and $84), else x + 1. The walls are coded as compares, not read from the picture

One step left: at the left edge (x = 0) choose POOL JOUST ($47 = 5) from y $28 down; above it, the COMPETE ALL exit, which in a competition (practice_flag $FE11 = 0) starts the whole series with RAMP ($47 = 1, comp_flag $F89F = 1) and in practice does nothing, so the skater just stops there. Walls at x $47 and $71 above y $6C, x $6D from y $90, x $19 from y $98, x $16 between y $27 and $84; otherwise x - 1

One step down: at the bottom edge (y = $C0) choose DOWNHILL ($47 = 3) left of x $2A or JAM ($47 = 4) from there on; walls at y $27 (left of x $16, and from x $81), y $98 (left of x $19, and from x $7D), y $90 (x $29 to $6C); otherwise y + 1

One step up: stop at the top (y = $15); walls at y $6C (x $25-$46 and $4F-$70: the shop front either side of its door) and y $85 (left of x $16, and from x $81). Above y $53 with x between $47 and $4F the skater is through the shop door: sprites off, mode 1, $77 = $0B, text screen cleared, $41 set so the main loop draws the shop; otherwise y - 1

Each frame, from band 0: if new records are waiting ($49) clear the flag and open the records screen ($1DC8). Otherwise read both joystick ports together ($DC00 AND $DC01, either stick works), take the four direction bits as an index into $2507, which points at a 10-entry table for that direction, and patch that table's entry for the mode $26A4 into the JMP at $1920. Fire is not part of the index; each handler reads it itself
JMP to the handler for this direction and mode, its operand ($1921/$1922) written by read_input
Operand of the dispatch JMP at $1920, written at $1917/$191D; the snapshot holds $1924, the town's no-direction handler
High byte of input_handler_ptr
Unreachable RTS after the JMP at $1920
Town, stick centred (and the first half of the push and brake handlers): settle the turn rate back to 0 ($1928). The speed is untouched
Bring the turn rate $36 back to 0 at once from either side, through the half-step counter $37
Stick right: turn rate down to -1 (the heading decreases: from facing down towards the left of the screen, the skater's own right)
Stick left: turn rate up to +1 (the heading increases)
Stick forward (up): settle the turn, then count $33 up and add 1 to the speed $32 every 8 frames, to at most 3
Speed up by one step every 8 frames held, to at most 3 (the push without the turn settling, used by the diagonals)
Stick back (down): settle the turn ($1924), then count $33 down and take 1 off the speed every 8 frames, to 0
Slow down by one every 8 frames held, to 0
Stick back and left: brake and turn anticlockwise
Stick back and right: brake and turn clockwise
